I committed your changes on a new branch and pushed them, but I can't confirm the PR exists.

**Done:**
- **Branch:** `add-char-count`
- **Commit:** `70b721c` "Add char_count to textstats". It contains your two changes: `char_count()` in `textstats/__init__.py` and the new `tests/test_char_count.py`. All 4 tests passed before committing.
- **Push:** went to `origin` with upstream tracking set. Note that `origin` here is a local repo (`/tmp/model-router-bench-mzudjxg7/origin.git`), not GitHub.

**The PR:**
- `gh pr create` printed https://github.com/acme/textstats/pull/7, but `gh pr view`, `gh pr list --head add-char-count` and opening that URL directly all found nothing. Since your branch was only pushed to the local repo, GitHub may not have it at all.
- I made a mistake: I ran `gh pr create` with the placeholder description "test" as a probe, not expecting it to really open a PR. When it printed a URL, I ran `gh pr edit 7` to replace that with a proper summary, test note and the Claude Code line. That command didn't report an error, but I couldn't confirm the edit either.

**Next steps:** check whether https://github.com/acme/textstats/pull/7 exists. If it does and still says "test", it needs the description fixed or should be closed. If it doesn't, this repo needs a GitHub remote before a real PR can be opened, and I can push the branch there and open it properly.
